slides.title: I love my design, but only when?
checks: Does every element on the screen deliver value?
Will the user achieve his goal with it?
Is it persona-checked?
What could make the design fail?
Does it meet UX metrics if any?

slides.title: Error states provided
slides.rationale: Bad error handling paired with useless error messages will make your visitors leave
checks: Are all forms and input fields error-handled?
What does the error page look like?
Can user recover from the error?

slides.title: Design system checked
slides.rationale: Consistency is key, and DS is the single source of truth
checks: Did you check if you reinvented elements that already exist in the design system?
Have you picked the right components as per the use case?
Did you introduce new font, icons, colors or shades of colors?

slides.title: Visual feedback on user actions
slides.rationale: When users click and nothing happens they will look for exit or click again.
checks: Have you considered adding microinteractions?
Did you use animation while content in loading up?

slides.title: Wording is awesome
checks: Do you speak the same language as your audience?
What do your users need to know on this screen?
Avoid jargons, and keep it short and simple that anybody can understand it easily

slides.title: Ready for test / review?
checks: Did you cover all scenarios to test journeys?
Did I replaced all dummy data with real data and removed all duplication?

slides.title: Developer handover prepared
slides.rationale: Make sure your developers have an effortless experience
checks: Make sure to write down every error state, blank state or animation placement.

attribution.title: Share & Critique your way to a Culture of Collaboration
attribution.author: Shalini Raghunathan
attribution.note: Third-party material. Not my work; a method I keep in the governance toolkit.

items: Have Shared context and/or work in related spaces

choreography.custodian: Custodian keeps time, facilitates the conversation, keeps it in scope.

stages.text: Collaborators ask for clarifications, if needed, briefly. 3-5 mins
Collaborators write feedback and post to the gallery in silence - 7-10 mins
stages.detail: Includes time for folks to read and react to others' comments.
Each collaborator reads out their post-its (and explains briefly, if needed). Nominates the next collaborator.

stages.text: Creator records Action Items and schedules follow-ups - 5 mins

Contextual: Share what the problem is and who are you solving it for.
Tell a story about your work's journey, inspirations and challenges.
Define scope. Where are you in the project and design lifecycle?
Concise: What aspects of the design work are you seeking feedback on?
What aspects of the design work do you NOT want feedback on?
Structure your narrative to precisely articulate why you are seeking feedback at this time.
Curious: Do not defend or solve. Feedback is a gift.
Listen to absorb and understand, not to respond.
Use "Why?" and "Yes, and..." to dig deeper and get the best out of the session.
Reflect and interpret. Translate feedback into action items that advance the work.

Contextual: Frame your feedback to focus on user's goals and objectives.
Stay within the scope of the feedback requested.
Critique the work, not the creator.
Concise: Provide feedback that is specific, objective and tangible.
Curious: Highlight what's working well. Don't focus only on the negatives.
State your assumptions. Ask for clarifications. Probe.
Challenge to contribute, not to win. Disagree respectfully.

Contextual: Ensure collaborators move through the 4 Players roles.
Remember and remind the group of the “Why”.

frameworks.name: I Like / I Wish / I Wonder
4 Ls Retrospective (adapted)
parts: What did the team long for?

readiness.must: When you can articulate your ideas visually and verbally.
nice: When you have strong opinions, loosely held, about your work.
When you have some clarity and some questions about your work.

dimensions.name: Discoverability
dimensions.definition: Allow user to quickly understand what the product offers and how to navigate through it

questions.text: Is your navigation clear and intuitive? Are you able to find the required entry points quickly? (Help, My claims, My Profile, etc.)
Does it assist you in quickly and easily locate information that you require? (quick links, search, help, etc.)

Is the layout clear and organized, making it easy for you to quickly understand and locate informatrion & features? (Information appearance, placement and order on landing page - Plan, benefits, vouchers, deals, and important quick entry points.

dimensions.name: Learnability
dimensions.definition: Minimize the time and effort required for users to become proficient in using the product

questions.text: Is the text easy to understand and convey just the right amount of information with no jargons? (Labels, headings, instructions, CTAs, etc.)

Is there a consistent design scheme across the product, where all the components and patterns look same and behave similarly? (Shape, color, position, and states of components like button, icon, textbox, dropdown, including drawer, gestures, micro-interaction, feedabck, toast message, layout, and navigation)

Does the visual design create a inviting impression to quickly understand the purpose of design elements and how to use the interface and navigate through its features. (Layout, buttons, icons, navigation, cards, input fields, links, gesture, that is widely recognized help users to interact effortlessly )

Are the design components familiar with clear visual cues (affordance) for you to quickly understand the purpose and how to interact with for action? (Buttons, icons, navigation, cards, input fields, text links, gesture, navigation that is widely recognized help users to interact effortlessly)

dimensions.name: Engagement
dimensions.definition: Captivate user attention and motivates them to explore and and assist in pursuing journey

questions.text: Is the UI aesthetically pleasing, with attractive visuals and appealing colors that capture users' attention and communicate the product's value and benefits. (Page composition, use of colors & typography, use of components, imageries, and interactivities)

Does it guide you through the journey with intuitive userflows and motivate you to complete tasks or reach your milestones? (Break jouneys into stages, Progressive disclosure, progress status, inline help to encourge , and feedback on the completion of tasks)

Did you notice any small animated effects while interacting with design elements, indicating that your action was recognised? ( Micro-intercations / animation - hover, progress Bar, button pressed, sound, transition effects, etc.)

Is the language familiar, easy, and persuasive enough to lessen cognitive load, establish an emotional connection, and inspire you to complete your tasks? (Labels, product info, headers, instructions, and messaging)

dimensions.name: Efficiency
dimensions.definition: Allow users to accomplish tasks quickly and with minimal efforts

questions.text: Do you see all the essential features or actions upfront, with prominent calls to action? And the remaining are called as on-demand basis. (Contextual navigation, view more, carousal, etc )

Are you able to complete the tasks efficiently within a few clicks? In the case of complex or long tasks, do you perform them in manageable steps? (Progressive disclosure, save draft , inline contextual help)
Do you get straightforward & simple instructions that guide you through tasks efficiently? (Instructions, inline help, textual clues, etc.
Did you receive any auto-assistance support to help you complete a task in less time? ( Auto-populating fields, predictive search, templatization, etc..)

dimensions.name: Error Handling & Guidance
dimensions.definition: Empower users and make them feel confident and capable while interacting with product

questions.text: Are you able to locate any support feature when you are lost and don't know what to do? (Help module, customer support, digital assistant, FAQ, etc.)

Are you guided through complex processes step by step to reduce the likelihood of getting lost and making mistakes? (Having relevent information and actions that facilites the jounery, provide inline contextual help, instant action validation, and show instructions to recover from error)
Are you assisted as and when you encounter errors and unfamiliar terms or actions? (Contextual help, tooltips, action oriented feedback)

Is the error message clear and descriptive to explain what went wrong and provide meaningful instructions on how to fix the issue? (Upload failed. Ensure the file is in PDF format that is under 5 MB, and try again.)
Are the graphics used as visual cues to warn about mistakes or errors meaningful and easy to understand ? (Field highlighting, error Icons, error color)

by_dimension.Discoverability: Complex navigation that users find confusing, leading to frustration and difficulty finding basic features.
by_dimension.Learnability: Users struggle to understand the design and instructions, resulting in difficulty knowing the purpose
by_dimension.Engagement: No interesting user flow (content & task) results in a lack of motivation to stay engaged.
by_dimension.Efficiency: Users find the system difficult to use, confusing, and frustrating.
by_dimension.Error Handling & Guidance: It's challenging for users to seek assistance when needed.

by_dimension.Discoverability: Users can navigate through after some trial and error, but they encounter challenges in locating specific settings.
by_dimension.Learnability: Users explore the interface before grasping how to complete tasks, leading to a moderate learning curve.
by_dimension.Engagement: User expereince with interactivities and challenges, leads to moderate engagement.
by_dimension.Efficiency: Users are able to complete tasks somehow; however, there were some difficulties or areas of confusion.
by_dimension.Error Handling & Guidance: Highlights errors after submission, but lacks clear instructions on how to correct the errors.

by_dimension.Discoverability: Users can easily find and understand the features, but some users need to search for the main CTAs button.
by_dimension.Learnability: Provides signifiers and instructions for various features, helping users understand the basics.
by_dimension.Engagement: Offers some level of personalization, encourages users to explore further.
by_dimension.Efficiency: Clearly stated instructions and layouts allow users to complete tasks without any major difficulties.
by_dimension.Error Handling & Guidance: Provides moderately helpful instructions that explain the purpose of specific tasks but don't offer a broader context.

by_dimension.Discoverability: Clean and intuitive design that allows users to quickly locate and access various features and settings.
by_dimension.Learnability: User-friendly interface, clearly labeled tools, and guided tutorials that make it easy for users to get started.
by_dimension.Engagement: Personalization that keeps users engaged by offering relevant and enjoyable content.
by_dimension.Efficiency: Intuitive navigation and streamlined tasks allow users to efficiently complete the tasks with minimal clicks and distractions.
by_dimension.Error Handling & Guidance: Assists users through a step-by-step wizard in completing tasks, reducing the chances of errors.

by_dimension.Discoverability: Prominently displays key functions, allowing users to work efficiently without confusion.
by_dimension.Learnability: Offers a series of guided exercises during onboarding, helping users understand how to use the app effectively from the start.
by_dimension.Engagement: Offers a blend of real-time updates, interactive features, and engaging content, keeping users actively involved.
by_dimension.Efficiency: Smart processing features and digital assistance, allowing users to swiftly perform tasks efficiently, save both time and effort.
by_dimension.Error Handling & Guidance: Comprehensive help center that includes articles, video tutorials, community forums, and direct support channels.
